messages.subject: Necessary inputs for mtpc only
parts:
Hi, 


I was wondering if the mtpc method can be used separately from the full brainGraph pipeline? If not, what analyses are necessary in order to run mtpc?


I have a number of adjacency matrices for two groups that were generated in matlab. The data represents PET values exported from a custom atlas using freesurfer. I would like to threshold the matrices using your multi-threshold permutation correction method. I have converted them to a list of igraph objects. However, I see from the example that there are several other arguments passed to brainGraph_GLM.


Thanks, 

Jonathan

messages.author: dadcb4fd6a01f8d1
messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] Necessary inputs for mtpc only
parts:
Hi Jonathan,

I describe the usage in Chapter 7 of my User Guide (you can download here if you haven't seen it yet: https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/s/wmupawb39bcdho3/brainGraph_UserGuide.pdf

Briefly,
* g.list: a list of lists of graphs. There should be 3 "levels" to the list, for (in order): group, threshold, subject
* thresholds: the numeric vector of thresholds applied to the raw connectivity matrices. I am unfamiliar with PET so I am not sure what this would be for your purposes. The actual values of this vector aren't important for any computations, so if you wanted, you could set it equal to 1:k (where k is the number of thresholds)
* N: the number of permutations (default = 500)
* perms: a "permute" object, which is essentially a matrix of the permutation order for all 1:N (default = NULL; i.e., you don't have to input anything for this, if you don't want to)
* alpha: the significance level (default = 0.05)

The remaining arguments are required for the calls to "brainGraph_GLM", and include:
* covars: a "data.table" of your covariates; this must have a column titled "Study.ID"
* measure: the graph measure you are interested in testing. If it happens to be, e.g., modularity, you would specify "mod"
* con.vec: an integer vector specifying your contrast of interest
* alt: the alternative hypothesis (default: two.sided)

There are others that are specific to building the design matrix, such as:
* coding (dummy, effects, or cell.means)
* mean.center (TRUE or FALSE)
* binarize (if you want to convert a factor into an integer vector)
* int (whether you want to include an interaction term)

Chapter 7 describes everything in great detail, but if there is anything I haven't explained well, please feel free to ask more questions.

Chris
